mainTopic: Shabbat 12a: The זב's pouch, תפילין before שבת, the lamplight decrees, lice, and visiting the sick on שבת
overview: The amud opens by finishing a debate about two ברייתות on a זב who goes out on שבת with his pouch (כיס): one says he is חייב, the other פטור. A comparison to water caught only to protect a wall fails, since the זב does want his pouch, and אביי ורבא resolve the contradiction as the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. Next, דבי רבי ישמעאל allows going out in תפילין on ערב שבת near dark, because a person must constantly be aware of his תפילין, learned by a קל וחומר from the ציץ. חנניא adds that one should check his clothes before שבת, which רב יוסף calls a great הלכה. The גמרא then proves from a ברייתא that the משנה's bans on delousing and reading by lamplight share one reason, שמא יטה, and שמואל extends the ban even to telling apart his clothes from his wife's, which רבא limits. Further rules about lice follow: no delousing in public out of dignity, a dispute on whether one may squeeze a louse on שבת, and the practices of several אמוראים. The amud ends with בית שמאי and בית הלל on killing a louse and on מצוה activities on שבת, and with what to say when visiting the sick on שבת.

steps.title: End of the cited source: water caught to protect the wall
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a source from מכשירין. Water collected only so the wall will not be damaged does not count as water placed on purpose ("כי יותן").
steps.simpleTranslation: [If one placed a vessel under a drip] so that the wall will not be damaged, [the water] is not considered under "כי יותן" (it does not make food susceptible to טומאה).
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining in the middle of a proof. The גמרא is finishing a quote from מכשירין, used to argue that the זב's pouch is not a significant use, just like water caught only to protect a wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that catching something only to avoid damage or mess is not a real, wanted use. If that is true for water, maybe it is also true for the זב's pouch. That would make the pouch insignificant and explain why one ברייתא says he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: "if [water] be placed": the פסוק that makes food able to become טמא only when it is wet with liquid a person wanted

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts mid-sentence. This line is the END of a quoted משנה being used as a comparison. It is not a new ruling about walls.

phrases.english: so that the wall should not be damaged —
phrases.notes: End of the quoted case from מכשירין

phrases.english: it is not under "if [water] be placed"!
phrases.notes: The water is not considered wanted

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁלֹּא יִלְקֶה הַכּוֹתֶל אֵינוֹ בְּכִי יוּתַּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a comparison begun on the previous amud, used to resolve the contradiction between the two ברייתות about the זב's pouch.
steps.raayaObject: The זב's pouch is not a significant use, so carrying it may be פטור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מכשירין: water caught only to protect a wall is not "כי יותן".

steps.title: The comparison fails: the זב actually wants his pouch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison. With the wall, the person does not want the water at all. The זב does want his pouch, to catch the discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are these comparable? There, he does not want those liquids at all. Here, he does want this pouch, to catch the discharge in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the wall case. It says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the wall case, the water is pure nuisance and the person wants nothing from it. The זב, however, really uses his pouch to collect the זיבה, because he needs to check whether he had a discharge. So the pouch is a wanted, purposeful object, and the proof falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: "Are they comparable?": a standard rejection formula

phrases.english: Are they comparable?
There, he does not want them —
these liquids, at all;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא קָא בָעֵי לֵיהּ לְהַאי כִּיס
phrases.english: here, he does want this pouch
phrases.notes: The זב has a real use for it

phrases.english: to catch the discharge in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison made in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The analogy between the wall-water case and the זב's pouch.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wall-owner wants nothing from the water, but the זב actively wants the pouch to collect the discharge.

steps.title: The pouch is really like the later clause: water inside the bowl
steps.stepSummary: The pouch matches the סיפא of the same משנה. Water that is already inside a bowl under a drip does count as "כי יותן", because once it is there the person wants it to stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is comparable only to the latter clause: A bowl into which a drip fell — water that splashes out or overflows is not under "כי יותן", but the water inside it is under "כי יותן".
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes further. It shows that the correct comparison is to the סיפא, which actually points the other way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the person never wanted the drip, once water is in the bowl he wants it to stay there and not mess the house, so it counts as wanted. The זב likewise wants the discharge to stay in the pouch. So the pouch is significant, and the original contradiction between the ברייתות comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: the latter clause of a משנה or ברייתא
a drip (of rain from the roof)
water that splashes out and water that overflows

steps.confusionAlert: Both clauses deal with unwanted dripping water. The difference is that water staying in the bowl is wanted where it is, while water splashing out is not.

phrases.english: This is comparable only to the latter clause:
a bowl into which a drip fell,
the water that splashes out and that overflows
is not under "if [water] be placed",
but the water inside it is under "if [water] be placed".
phrases.notes: He wants it to stay in the bowl

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the rejection by showing which clause the pouch really matches.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole attempt to treat the pouch as insignificant.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The pouch resembles the water inside the bowl, which counts as wanted, so the proposed resolution fails.

steps.title: אביי ורבא: the two ברייתות follow רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: אביי ורבא resolve the contradiction as a מחלוקת. The ברייתא that says חייב follows רבי יהודה. The one that says פטור follows רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is אביי and רבא who both said: It is not difficult. This one follows רבי יהודה, and that one follows רבי שמעון.
steps.whatsHappening: After the earlier attempt failed, the גמרא gives the accepted answer. The two ברייתות simply follow two different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The זב does not really want the carrying for its own sake. He would prefer to have no discharge at all. This is a מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה. רבי יהודה holds a person is חייב for such a מלאכה, while רבי שמעון holds he is פטור, so each ברייתא matches one view.

keyTerms.meaning: "it is not difficult": the contradiction is resolved
a forbidden act done not for its own purpose (the background concept here)

steps.whatToRemember: The contradiction about the זב's pouch is resolved as the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה (חייב) and רבי שמעון (פטור) about מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This connects a small case, a זב's pouch, to one of the most important principles in הלכות שבת.

phrases.english: Rather, it is אביי and רבא
who both said: it is not difficult:

phrases.aramaic: הָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, וְהָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: this one is רבי יהודה, and that one is רבי שמעון.
phrases.notes: חייב follows רבי יהודה; פטור follows רבי שמעון

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אַבָּיֵי וְרָבָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ לָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected resolution with a new, accepted one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing each source to a different תנא (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתות contradict each other unless the pouch can be shown to be insignificant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות stand. They reflect the מחלוקת of רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about מלאכה שאינה צריכה לגופה.

steps.title: A person may go out wearing תפילין on ערב שבת near dark
steps.stepSummary: דבי רבי ישמעאל teaches that one may go out wearing תפילין on ערב שבת close to nightfall, without worrying he will end up carrying them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: A person may go out wearing תפילין on ערב שבת at nightfall.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that allows going out in תפילין right before שבת starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally there is a worry that someone will forget and carry an item once שבת begins. Here the ברייתא allows it with תפילין. The question of why comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי ישמעאל taught (a ברייתא)

phrases.english: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
A person may go out wearing תפילין
on ערב שבת at nightfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic on the related theme of forgetting and carrying on Shabbat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may go out wearing תפילין on ערב שבת near dark.

steps.title: Why is it allowed?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why we are not worried that he will forget the תפילין and carry them on שבת. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the usual worry about forgetting. It asks what makes תפילין different.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why there is no concern that he will forget and carry the תפילין on שבת.

steps.title: One must constantly touch his תפילין
steps.stepSummary: The answer is based on רבה בר רב הונא, who says a person must touch his תפילין all the time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because רבה בר רב הונא said: A person is obligated to touch his תפילין every single hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that someone wearing תפילין is required to keep feeling them, so he stays aware of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he is always checking his תפילין, he will not forget they are on his head. That removes the worry of carrying them into שבת by mistake.

phrases.aramaic: — כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
phrases.english: — Because רבה בר רב הונא said:
A person is obligated to touch his תפילין
every single hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because one must constantly touch his תפילין, he remembers them.

steps.title: The source: a קל וחומר from the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: The obligation to stay aware of תפילין is learned by a קל וחומר from the ציץ of the כהן גדול. The ציץ has one שם השם, and the תורה still requires constant awareness of it. תפילין have many, so all the more so.
steps.simpleTranslation: A קל וחומר from the ציץ: The ציץ has only one mention of השם, and the תורה said "and it shall be on his forehead always", meaning he may not take his mind off it. תפילין, which have many mentions of השם, all the more so.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבה בר רב הונא's rule, using a קל וחומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תמיד" (always) by the ציץ is read as a requirement of constant awareness. The more holy names an item contains, the more attention it deserves. So תפילין, with many names, need constant awareness even more.

keyTerms.meaning: an argument from a lighter case to a stricter one
the gold forehead-plate of the כהן גדול
that he not take his mind off it

phrases.english: An a fortiori argument from the ציץ:

phrases.aramaic: מָה צִיץ שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ אֶלָּא אַזְכָּרָה אַחַת
phrases.english: Just as the ציץ, which has only one mention of השם —
the תורה said "and it shall be on his forehead always" —
meaning that he should not take his mind off it;
תפילין, which have many mentions of השם —
how much more so.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבה בר רב הונא's rule in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: One must constantly be aware of his תפילין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק "והיה על מצחו תמיד" about the ציץ, via קל וחומר.

steps.title: Therefore he will remember the תפילין
steps.stepSummary: Because he is always aware of his תפילין, he will remember them and not carry them on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, he certainly remembers them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ties the answer back to the ברייתא. Since he keeps remembering the תפילין, going out in them before שבת is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the loop. The duty of constant awareness is exactly what removes the fear of forgetting.
steps.whatToRemember: One may go out in תפילין near שבת because a person must constantly be aware of them (קל וחומר from the ציץ), so he will not forget them.

phrases.english: Therefore, he surely remembers them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the derived rule back to the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no concern of forgetting תפילין, so going out in them on ערב שבת near dark is allowed.

steps.title: חנניא: check your clothing before Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: חנניא teaches that a person must feel his clothes on ערב שבת near dark, so he does not carry something by mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: חנניא says: A person must feel his clothing on ערב שבת at nightfall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related ברייתא. Before שבת, a person should check his pockets and clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same worry of forgetting and carrying on שבת. Here the fix is a check before שבת, so nothing is left in his pockets.

phrases.english: It was taught: חנניא says:
A person must feel his clothing
on ערב שבת at nightfall.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Related teaching, also about touching or checking to avoid carrying on Shabbat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One must check his clothing on ערב שבת near dark.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a great הלכה for שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף praises חנניא's rule as an important הלכה for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is a great הלכה for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף comments on חנניא's teaching and stresses how important it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Checking one's clothes is a simple step, but it prevents a real איסור of carrying. So רב יוסף calls it a great הלכה.
steps.whatToRemember: Checking your pockets before שבת is a significant practice that prevents accidental carrying.

phrases.english: רב יוסף said:
It is a great הלכה for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף הִלְכְתָא רַבָּתִי לְשַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on and endorses step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: חנניא's rule of checking one's clothing before שבת is an important הלכה.

steps.title: Is delousing forbidden by day too, or only by lamplight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids delousing. Is it out of fear of killing a louse, following רבי אליעזר, which would apply even by day? Or is it, like reading, out of fear of tilting the lamp, which applies only at night?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'He may not delouse his clothes, etc.' The question was asked: Does this mean he may not delouse his clothes even by day, in case he kills a louse, and our משנה follows רבי אליעזר? For a ברייתא teaches that רבי אליעזר said: killing a louse on שבת is like killing a camel. Then the rule 'he may not read by lamplight' would be a separate rule, in case he tilts the lamp. Or perhaps both rules are because he might tilt the lamp?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and raises a question about it. Are the two rules next to each other in the משנה, delousing and reading, based on the same reason or on two different reasons?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one says delousing is banned because he might kill a louse. That is a real שבת prohibition according to רבי אליעזר, so the ban would apply all day, even in daylight. Side two says both rules share one worry, שמא יטה, tilting the lamp to get more light. Then delousing would only be banned at night by a lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: Check clothing for lice and remove them
A question was asked among the Sages (a real open question)
In case he tilts the lamp (to bring the oil closer to the wick, which is like kindling)
Or perhaps (introduces the second side of a question)

steps.confusionAlert: The key word in the question is בַּיּוֹם, 'by day'. If the reason is killing a louse, delousing is banned even in daylight. If the reason is the lamp, it is only banned at night.

phrases.english: 'He may not delouse his clothes, etc.'
It was asked of them:
Does it mean he may not delouse his clothes even by day
in case he kills a louse,
and the משנה follows רבי אליעזר?
For it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי אליעזר said:
One who kills a louse on Shabbat
is as if he killed a camel.
phrases.notes: Size does not matter; killing a tiny creature is also forbidden.

phrases.english: And 'he may not read by lamplight'
is a separate rule, in case he tilts the lamp.
Or perhaps both rules are because he might tilt the lamp?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from חנניא's teaching to the next line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the reason for banning delousing the fear of killing a louse, which would apply even by day, or the fear of tilting the lamp, which applies only at night?

steps.title: First proof: a ברייתא lists both rules together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says 'we do not delouse and we do not read by lamplight'. It suggests that 'by lamplight' covers both rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'We do not delouse and we do not read by lamplight.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question with a ברייתא. In the ברייתא, the words 'by lamplight' seem to apply to delousing as well as reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'by lamplight' refers to both actions, then delousing is only banned at night by a lamp. That would mean the reason is שמא יטה, not killing a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: By the light of the lamp

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין פּוֹלִין וְאֵין קוֹרִין לְאוֹר הַנֵּר.
phrases.english: We do not delouse and we do not read by lamplight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to settle the question from step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That both rules are because of שמא יטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that lists delousing and reading together, followed by 'by lamplight'.

steps.title: Rejected: the ברייתא is no clearer than the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The ברייתא lists the two rules together just as the משנה does, and that was not enough to answer the question there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this ברייתא any stronger than our משנה?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 13. This ברייתא tells us nothing the משנה did not already tell us.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה also put delousing and reading side by side, and we still had a question. A ברייתא with the same wording has the same ambiguity. 'By lamplight' could still refer only to reading.

phrases.english: Is it any stronger than our משנה?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the first ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא has the same ambiguous wording as the משנה, so it cannot resolve the question.

steps.title: Second proof: 'by lamplight' is said about each rule
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא repeats 'by lamplight' separately for delousing and for reading. It also says these were among the decrees made in the upper room of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'We do not delouse by lamplight and we do not read by lamplight. These are among the rules they said in the upper room of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. This one clearly attaches 'by lamplight' to delousing on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is better than the first ברייתא because it says 'by lamplight' twice, once for each rule. So delousing is clearly tied to the lamp, and the worry must be tilting the lamp, not killing a louse.

keyTerms.meaning: Rules, here the famous decrees made by the Sages

keyTerms.term: עֲלִיַּית חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה בֶּן גָּרוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: The upper room of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון, where eighteen famous decrees were made

phrases.english: Come and hear:
We do not delouse by lamplight
and we do not read by lamplight,
these are among the rules that they said

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲלִיַּית חֲנַנְיָה בֶּן חִזְקִיָּה בֶּן גָּרוֹן.
phrases.english: in the upper room of חנניה בן חזקיה בן גרון.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was rejected, brings a clearer source.
steps.raayaObject: That delousing is banned only by lamplight, because of שמא יטה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says 'by lamplight' separately for each rule.

steps.title: Conclusion: both rules are about tilting the lamp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both delousing and reading are banned because of שמא יטה. So delousing by day is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn from this that both are because he might tilt the lamp. Indeed, learn from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the second proof and closes the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is settled on the second side. The משנה does not follow רבי אליעזר's worry about killing a louse. Delousing is only a problem at night by a lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this (the proof is accepted)

steps.whatToRemember: Delousing (לא יפלה) and reading by lamplight share the same reason, שמא יטה. During the day, delousing is not banned by this rule.

phrases.english: Learn from this
that both are because he might tilt the lamp;
indeed, learn from this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the proof from step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rules are rooted in שמא יטה and apply only by lamplight.

steps.title: Even sorting his clothes from his wife's is forbidden by lamplight
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, in the name of שמואל, teaches that one may not use lamplight even just to tell apart his clothes from his wife's.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Even to tell apart his clothes from his wife's clothes is forbidden by lamplight.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement widens the ban on using a lamp on שבת night. It now includes a small, quick task.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think only long, focused tasks like reading lead to tilting the lamp. שמואל says even a short task that needs a careful look counts. While trying to see better, he might tilt the lamp.

phrases.english: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל:
Even to distinguish
between his clothes and his wife's clothes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the lamplight rule and extends its reach.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Using lamplight even to tell apart men's and women's clothes is forbidden on שבת night.

steps.title: רבא limits it to the people of מחוזא
steps.stepSummary: רבא says שמואל's rule applies only in מחוזא, where men's and women's clothes look alike. Farm people's clothes are easy to tell apart.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We only said this about the people of מחוזא. But farm people know the difference easily.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא narrows שמואל's rule from step 17 to a specific place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry only exists when he has to look closely. In wealthy מחוזא, men's clothes were fancy like women's, so they were hard to tell apart. Village farmers' clothes are clearly different, so there is no need to strain and no fear of tilting the lamp.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this about (introduces a limitation)
מחוזא, a wealthy city in Babylonia

phrases.english: רבא said:
We only said this regarding the people of מחוזא,
but regarding farm people,
they know the difference easily.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits שמואל's rule from step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל's ban applies only where the clothes are hard to tell apart, as in מחוזא.

steps.title: Even in מחוזא, only old women's clothes are a problem
steps.stepSummary: רבא narrows further. Even in מחוזא, the rule applies only to old women's clothes, which look like men's. Young women's clothes are easy to recognize.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even about the people of מחוזא, we only said this about old women's clothes. But young women's clothes are easy to recognize.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a second, narrower limit to שמואל's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same logic applies again: the ban exists only when telling the clothes apart takes effort. Older women wore plainer clothes that looked like the men's. Young women's colorful clothes are obvious, so there is no worry.
steps.whatToRemember: The lamplight ban applies whenever a task needs a careful look, even a quick one, because he might tilt the lamp. It does not apply where the difference is obvious.

phrases.english: And even regarding the people of מחוזא,
we only said this regarding old women's clothes,
but regarding young women's clothes,
they know the difference easily.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְדִבְנֵי מָחוֹזָא נָמֵי לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דִּזְקֵנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבא's limitation from step 18 even further.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In מחוזא, the ban applies only to telling apart men's clothes from old women's clothes.

steps.title: No delousing clothes in public
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that you may not delouse your clothes in a public place, because it is undignified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: You may not delouse clothes in a public place, out of respect for people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps the topic of delousing going. It brings a ברייתא that forbids doing it where people can see.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule has nothing to do with שבת. Delousing in front of others is disgusting to see, so it is banned out of respect for people. It applies on any day.

keyTerms.meaning: Delousing; shaking or picking lice off clothing
Out of respect for human dignity

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not delouse clothes in a public place
out of respect for people.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין פּוֹלִין בִּרְשׁוּת הָרַבִּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the topic of delousing from the lamplight discussion and adds a rule about doing it in public.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Delousing in public is forbidden out of respect for human dignity.

steps.title: No taking an emetic in public
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, or some say רבי נחמיה, gives a similar rule: you may not take a vomit-inducing drug in public, for the same reason of dignity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Similarly, רב יהודה said, and some say it was רבי נחמיה: You may not take an emetic in a public place, out of respect for people.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second rule that works the same way as the first. You may not make yourself vomit in public.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word כיוצא בו tells us this rule follows the same logic as the delousing rule. Both acts are disgusting for others to watch. The גמרא is not sure who said it, so it names two possible speakers.

keyTerms.meaning: An emetic; a drug that makes a person vomit

phrases.english: Similarly, Rav Yehuda said,
and some say it was Rabbi Neḥemya:
One may not take an emetic in a public place
out of respect for people.
phrases.notes: Same reason as the delousing rule.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a parallel case that uses the same reason of dignity.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking an emetic in public is forbidden out of respect for human dignity.

steps.title: Squeeze the louse and throw it, but do not kill it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that someone delousing his clothes on שבת may squeeze a louse and throw it away, as long as he does not kill it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Someone who delouses his clothes may squeeze the louse and throw it away, as long as he does not kill it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks how you may get rid of a louse on שבת. This is the first opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Killing the louse is the problem on שבת. According to this view, squeezing it is fine because squeezing is not killing. You just must not go so far as to kill it.

keyTerms.meaning: Squeezes or rubs between the fingers
As long as he does not

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who delouses his clothes
may squeeze the louse and throw it away,
as long as he does not kill it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from delousing in public to how you may handle a louse on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת you may squeeze a louse and throw it away, but you may not kill it.

steps.title: אבא שאול: you may not even squeeze it
steps.stepSummary: אבא שאול is stricter: you may pick up the louse and throw it away, but you may not squeeze it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבא שאול says: He may pick the louse up and throw it away, as long as he does not squeeze it.
steps.whatsHappening: אבא שאול disagrees with the first opinion. He forbids squeezing too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אבא שאול holds that killing a louse on שבת is an איסור דאורייתא. So he forbids squeezing as well, in case squeezing ends up killing it. The only thing he allows is picking it up and throwing it away.

phrases.english: Abba Shaul says: He may pick it up and throw it away,
as long as he does not squeeze it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different, stricter opinion in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שבת you may only pick up the louse and throw it away. Even squeezing is forbidden.

steps.title: רב הונא rules: squeeze and throw, even on a weekday
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules like the first opinion: you may squeeze and throw. He adds that this is the dignified way to deal with a louse, even on a weekday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The law is that he squeezes and throws it away. That is the dignified way, even on a weekday.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא decides the dispute in favor of the first opinion. He also gives advice that applies on weekdays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ruling follows the more lenient view, so squeezing is allowed on שבת. רב הונא then adds that even on a weekday, when killing is allowed, it is more dignified to squeeze and throw. Killing a louse with your hands is disgusting.

keyTerms.meaning: And that is the dignified way

steps.confusionAlert: The words 'even on a weekday' do not mean killing a louse is forbidden on a weekday. They mean that squeezing and throwing is the cleaner, more dignified way to do it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה מוֹלֵל וְזוֹרֵק
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: The law is that he squeezes and throws,
and that is the dignified way, even on a weekday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה מוֹלֵל וְזוֹרֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the dispute between the first opinion and אבא שאול.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The law follows the first opinion: squeeze and throw. This is also the dignified way on weekdays.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling on how to handle lice on שבת.

steps.title: רבה and רב ששת killed lice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reports that רבה and רב ששת would kill lice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה would kill the lice. And רב ששת would kill them too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now reports what some אמוראים actually did with lice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These two great rabbis killed lice directly. Their practice shows that some did not follow רב הונא's advice to only squeeze and throw. They may have held that killing a louse is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Would kill them (literally, cut them up)

phrases.english: Rabba would kill them.
And Rav Sheshet would kill them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ruling, reports what rabbis actually did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה and רב ששת would kill lice.

steps.title: רבא threw lice into water
steps.stepSummary: רבא would throw lice into a cup of water instead of killing them with his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would throw them into a cup of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives another rabbi's practice. רבא did not kill the lice with his hands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing lice into water gets rid of them without killing them directly. This is a middle path between killing and only throwing them away.

phrases.english: Rava would throw them into a cup of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another reported practice, different from killing them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבא disposed of lice by throwing them into water.

steps.title: רב נחמן told his daughters to kill lice
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן told his daughters to kill the lice and to let him hear the combs at work.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to his daughters: Kill them, and let me hear the sound of the combs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the list of practices with רב נחמן, who openly told his daughters to kill lice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן not only allowed killing lice, he wanted to hear it being done. This shows he held that killing them in the normal way, on the comb, was completely fine.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said to his daughters:
Kill them, and let me hear the sound of the combs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last reported practice, and the most lenient one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב נחמן encouraged killing lice in the usual way.

steps.title: בית שמאי and בית הלל on killing a louse on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר reports a dispute: בית שמאי forbid killing a louse on שבת, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: One may not kill a louse on שבת. This is the view of בית שמאי. And בית הלל permit it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the basic source about killing a louse on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that a louse is different from other creatures that you may not kill on שבת, so killing it is allowed. This is a separate, basic source on the שבת question. The גמרא does not present it as the reason behind the reported practices of רבה, רב ששת, רבא and רב נחמן.
steps.whatToRemember: According to בית הלל, killing a louse on שבת is allowed, while בית שמאי forbid it.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
One may not kill a louse on Shabbat,
this is the view of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel permit it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the basic source on whether one may kill a louse on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי forbid killing a louse on שבת. בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: מצוה activities on שבת: בית שמאי forbid, בית הלל permit
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, quoting רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, lists activities that בית שמאי forbid on שבת and בית הלל permit: arranging a match, arranging a child's schooling or trade training, comforting mourners, and visiting the sick.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי שמעון בן אלעזר also said in the name of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: One may not arrange a match for children to get betrothed, or arrange for a child to learn to read or to learn a trade, or comfort mourners, or visit the sick on שבת. This is the view of בית שמאי. And בית הלל permit all of these.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted the same speaker, it adds another dispute between בית שמאי and בית הלל that he reported.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי see these activities as weekday business that does not belong on שבת. בית הלל permit them because each one is a מצוה. The last item, visiting the sick, leads into the next step.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar would also say
in the name of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel:
One may not arrange matches for children to betroth them,
nor arrange for a child to be taught to read
or to be taught a trade,
and one may not comfort mourners,
and one may not visit the sick on Shabbat,
this is the view of Beit Shammai.
And Beit Hillel permit them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings another teaching by the same speaker, on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל permit מצוה activities on שבת, like arranging matches and schooling, comforting mourners, and visiting the sick. בית שמאי forbid them.

steps.title: What to say when visiting the sick on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a visitor to a sick person on שבת says: 'It is שבת, when we do not cry out, and healing will come soon.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: One who comes to visit a sick person says: 'It is שבת, when we may not cry out, and healing will come soon.'
steps.whatsHappening: Now that visiting the sick on שבת is allowed, the גמרא teaches what the visitor should say.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת we do not cry out in prayer the way we do on a weekday. So the visitor mentions that it is שבת and offers a hopeful word that healing is near, instead of a full weekday prayer.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, הַנִּכְנָס לְבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: One who comes to visit a sick person says:
'It is Shabbat, when we may not cry out,
and healing will come soon.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן, הַנִּכְנָס לְבַקֵּר אֶת הַחוֹלֶה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on בית הלל's ruling that you may visit the sick on שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A visitor on שבת says: 'It is שבת, when we do not cry out, and healing will come soon.'

steps.title: רבי מאיר: שבת itself can bring compassion
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says the visitor should add that שבת itself has the power to bring mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר says: 'It, שבת, can bring compassion.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר gives a different or added wording for what the visitor says.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of focusing only on not crying out, רבי מאיר stresses the merit of שבת. The holiness of the day can itself bring God's mercy to the sick person.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל allow visiting the sick on שבת. The visitor speaks gently, without weekday crying out, and may mention the healing power of שבת.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Meir says:
'It, Shabbat, can bring compassion.'

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: יְכוֹלָה הִיא שֶׁתְּרַחֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another wording for the visitor's words.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The visitor should say that the merit of שבת can bring compassion.
